items.abstract: <jats:p>The field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been on a transformative era as traditional pre-training paradigms, reliant on vast amounts of high-quality data, face the inevitable constraints, herein dubbed "peak data". This paper explores the implications of a "post-pre-training" era, where AI systems are envisioned to transcend static data dependency and evolve into agentic AI (aAI) entities capable of autonomous decision-making, beyond pattern recognition, dynamic interaction with their environments, and advanced reasoning akin to human cognitive processes.</jats:p>
title: The end of Pre-Training for LLMs: The Future of Agentic and AI Reasoning Beyond Peak Data

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:p>Agentic reasoning systems increasingly interact with environments whose states are only partially observed, dynamically evolving, and constrained by physical, biological, or logical structure. Existing agentic reasoning frameworks often model internal reasoning, tool use, and post-training adaptation using flat latent representations and struggle in curved manifold space environments. However, many scientific and embodied domains naturally lie on curved state spaces, including tissue geometry, developmental trajectories, protein conformations, robotic configuration spaces, and constrained physical systems. We introduce Manifold Agentic Reasoning, a geometric framework that extends agentic reasoning from Euclidean latent spaces to Riemannian manifolds. In the proposed framework, observations are encoded as manifold-valued states, memory is retrieved by geodesic similarity, candidate hypotheses are generated in tangent spaces, predicted transitions are projected by exponential maps, and decisions are admitted through verification-gated commitment or repaired by manifold self-correction. We further extend the framework to graph-agentic manifold reasoning, where node states live on manifolds and neighbor information is transported by logarithmic maps before attention-based aggregation. Manifold agent reasoning moves AI past brittle, prompt-chained templates to solve four critical production flaws: silent hallucinations and reasoning drift, brittle tool and context misuse, the black-box evaluation problem and stiff behavior profiles.</jats:p>
                <jats:p>To evaluate the framework, we introduce a Curved Tissue Manipulation and Recovery benchmark in which an agent must repair damaged tissue on a curved manifold. Simulated results show that the full manifold-agent substantially outperforms both a baseline reasoning agent and a full flat-agent reasoning system, achieving higher recovery success, lower geodesic shape error, lower pattern error, and fewer invalid transitions. Curvature and ablation studies indicate that the performance gain is driven by geometry-aware reasoning, verification, memory, and self-repair. These results suggest that manifold-aware agentic reasoning provides a principled foundation for reliable scientific and embodied AI systems operating in curved, constrained, or mechanistic domains.</jats:p>
title: Manifold Agentic Reasoning: Extending Agentic POMDPs and Post-Training Reasoning to Riemannian State and Reasoning Spaces

<jats:p>Abstract:
This consolidated research book develops an integrated architecture for reasoning about two classes of systems that are usually studied separately: path-dependent financial markets and multiscale Earth-system dynamics. It links rough-volatility reasoning, signature-based representations, deep hedging and generative market simulation with quantum topological data analysis, carbon-state modelling, climate-risk prediction and policy-oriented digital twins. The central proposition is that both domains require methods capable of representing nonstationarity, multiscale dependence, tail behaviour, regime shifts, nonlinear feedback and uncertainty in decisions that must remain auditable under changing conditions. The book therefore organizes statistical explanation, causal inference, machine learning, topological representation, reinforcement learning, scalable data engineering and governance within a single reproducible research lifecycle. Five chapters progress from foundations and uncertainty to causal modelling, predictive intelligence, MLOps-scale implementation and sectoral governance. A dedicated thematic synthesis then develops ten research agendas for agentic financial reasoning using only the supplied reference corpus and Harvard-style in-text citations. The resulting framework is designed for researchers, financial institutions, climate-risk teams, regulators, infrastructure operators and public agencies seeking interoperable decision systems that connect market resilience, carbon integrity, climate adaptation and responsible AI.
Keywords
agentic financial reasoning, rough volatility, signature methods, deep hedging, generative market simulation, systemic risk, causal inference, quantum topological data analysis, persistent homology, Earth-system intelligence, carbon dynamics, climate-risk prediction, digital twins, physics-informed learning, reinforcement learning, foundation models, big-data engineering, MLOps, model risk, carbon MRV, climate finance, governance, responsible AI</jats:p>
title: Agentic Financial Reasoning with Rough Volatility, Signature-Based Learning, Deep Hedging and Generative Market Simulation
EigentSearch-Q+: Enhancing Deep Research Agents with Structured Reasoning Tools
